Pressing the second button, 4x+1, appends the bits "01" to the binary form of x. Pressing the first button, ⌊x/2⌋, deletes the last bit. Starting from 0, every reachable number therefore has a binary representation with no two adjacent 1s, and every such number can be reached. (I am relying on the standard characterization for this problem and have not rebuilt the reachability proof here.)

Count the numbers below 2048 = 2¹¹ whose binary form has no two adjacent 1s. Allowing leading zeros, the number of 11-bit strings with no two adjacent 1s is F₁₃ = 233, where F₁ = F₂ = 1. This count includes 0.

The largest such 11-bit number is 10101010101₂ = 1365, which is below 2014. So all 233 numbers satisfy the bound, and the numbers above 2014 are not an issue.

ANSWER: 233
